In addtion, there other other places add comma like `tidb/store/copr/coprocessor.go`

```go
func (worker *copIteratorWorker) logTimeCopTask(costTime time.Duration, task *copTask, bo *Backoffer, resp *tikvrpc.Response) {
	logStr := fmt.Sprintf("[TIME_COP_PROCESS] resp_time:%s txnStartTS:%d region_id:%d store_addr:%s", costTime, worker.req.StartTs, task.region.GetID(), task.storeAddr)
	if bo.GetTotalSleep() > minLogBackoffTime {
		backoffTypes := strings.Replace(fmt.Sprintf("%v", bo.TiKVBackoffer().GetTypes()), " ", ",", -1)
		logStr += fmt.Sprintf(" backoff_ms:%d backoff_types:%s", bo.GetTotalSleep(), backoffTypes)
	}
```

Idea: As our [doc](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidb/stable/identify-slow-queries#parse-tidb-slow-logs-with-pt-query-digest) suggests to use pt-query-digest to parse the slow query, how about we *additionally* ensure compatibility with it?

@crazycs520

review_comments:
```
Backoff_types: [tikvRPC,regionMiss,tikvRPC,regionMiss,tikvRPC,regionMiss,tikvRPC,regionMiss,tikvRPC,regionMiss,tikvRPC,regionMiss,tikvRPC,regionMiss,tikvRPC,regionMiss,tikvRPC,regionMiss,tikvRPC,regionMiss]
```

Actually, there are only 2 kinds of backoff: `regionMiss` and `regionMiss`, there are too much duplicate information. So I want to change the output to `backoff_type*count`:

```sql
Backoff_types: [tikvRPC*10,regionMiss*10]
``` 

And if the count is 1, just ignore it, such as:

```sql
Backoff_types: [tikvRPC*10,regionMiss*10,pdRPC]
``` 

@bb7133 @breeswish what do you think?
Maybe order by the count with desc is easier to read.

It does look Great, but what i worried is that the compatibility maybe broken more, which will amplify the radius of damage. @crazycs520 
like this line:
https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/blob/e5bf177cd91ad689176c5f647e1e37d5cd47899c/util/stmtsummary/statement_summary.go#L763
```go
		ssElement.sumBackoffTimes += int64(len(commitDetails.Mu.BackoffTypes))
		for _, backoffType := range commitDetails.Mu.BackoffTypes {
			ssElement.backoffTypes[backoffType] += 1
		}
```
why this change will affect this?

Aha~ My mistake, `BackoffTypes` here seems got from stats in memory instead of slow.log.  this case is not suitable, what I mean is that some tools like `pt-query-digest` or some application on table `slow_query` may be a little confused, since the semantic of `backofftypes` means a list of backoff type.

BTW, I am not very sure what's the purpose of the backoffTypes shown in slow log. 🤣

```sql
Backoff_types: [tikvRPC regionMiss]
```

For the old version of slow log, the parse will still be wrong, I think we should fix this too.
It sounds reasonable for compatibility, but does it really happen that the new parser working on the old version of slow log? 🤔
It will happen, after TiDB upgrades to the new version, it still can parse the old slow log. The old slow log will not be removed unless the human manual deletes it.

Sounds like we can match `xxxx:` to distinguish fields.

IMO, we may also need some regression tests to verify that the slow log can be correctly parsed by percona tools.
match `xxxx:` to distinguish fields is a great idea. I like it.

> Sounds like we can match `xxxx:` to distinguish fields.
> 
> IMO, we may also need some regression tests to verify that the slow log can be correctly parsed by percona tools.

LGTM, I will add this pattern.
I made another solution about this #28160 , but I am not sure if it is better since it used `regex`.  @crazycs520 @breeswish
What if we make both parser exits, when ',' exits, we used the new parser. To old version, we use the regex parser with little perf loss.🤔 Not elegant, but works. @crazycs520

@crazycs520 @bb7133  @breeswish 
I think about the solution once again. I prefer the `comma added` solution, reasons are like that:
1. clear format makes it easy to parse by other tools, which makes code and performance better.
2. compatibility problem above is a small probability event, and even it happens, we can easily solve it by `flush logs`.
3. slow log can rotate by the default config, which makes the little bug disappear when time goes on.
4. In the long run, the terrible format of the slow log may bring more pain to us.
